proposed_global_claims.statement: For every finite full B-module M0 in L, finite generation of its differential saturation forces absence of height-one ramification.
The normalization-seed differential saturation is finite if and only if the finite normalization is unramified in codimension one.

Because the normalization is finite over the target, every divisorial source boundary maps onto a height-one base divisor; ramified pole stages and genuine positive unramified pole stages have nonfinite saturation.
At a generic height-one point of the full finite-cover permutation connection, an embedded ordinary coherent lattice exists if and only if local inertia is trivial.
Regular holonomicity and coherent logarithmic extension do not imply ordinary structure-sheaf finiteness or translation stability.

Derive trivial height-one inertia from the polynomial Keller source; a direct global D-module route additionally requires global ordinary coherence with a compatible connection preserving both unscaled translations, and a torsion-free meromorphic embedding with generic fiber L.

The audited dual, canonical, intersection, jet, and cohomological constructions do not bypass the inertia bridge; the finite-seed obstruction applies only to full intersections, and multiplier stability is a separate stable-order condition.

proposed_graph_nodes.statement: The finite-full-seed and normalization-saturation routes exclude height-one ramification, while the local D-module route reduces to trivial height-one inertia; logarithmic or holonomic coherence is insufficient, and the direct global D-module route also needs an embedded ordinary coherent extension with a compatible connection preserving both unscaled translations.
